outlook.statement: Aim to once again reach peak revenue of Rs 500 Crore by Financial Year 2028, with much better profitability and stronger financials. Cautiously expand exclusive retail presence coupled with E-Commerce and Deepening Distribution to drive revenue scale up. Focus on profitable growth, disciplined execution, continuous improvement, strengthening margins and cash flows.

Continued expansion in MBO, franchise-led, and omni-channel formats is expected to support scalable and profitable growth. Ongoing focus on inventory optimisation, working capital discipline, and cost efficiencies is expected to further strengthen margins and cash flows. Product innovation, enhanced customer engagement, and focused brand-building initiatives are expected to improve brand visibility and demand momentum. Management remains cautiously optimistic on industry growth prospects, supported by premiumisation trends, improving retail sentiment, and increasing organised retail penetration.

The worldwide economy illustrated measured strength in 2025, exploring a challenging scene characterized by geopolitical pressures, lifted interest rates, and diligent supply-side weights. World GDP developed by 3.4 percent in 2025 and is anticipated to extend by 3.1 percent and 3.2 percent in 2026 and 2027 individually. The 2026 calendar year marks a major departure from traditional retail forecasting toward tech-driven, hyper-localized execution models. AI-Driven Trend Forecasting & Supply Chain Optimization has successfully reduced inventory deadstock by up to 50%, shifting production toward localized, agile batches. Gen-Z consumers are actively rejecting rigid corporate brand-chasing.

The Indian apparel industry in FY 2026 is positioned at a structural inflection point, transitioning from price-driven mass consumption to a brand-conscious, digitally enabled, and experience-driven market. For a mid-premium apparel segment, the outlook remains positive but competitively intense.

The domestic apparel market is projected to scale from a base of USD 88 Billion to USD 117 Billion by 2034. The trajectory of the Indian Apparel Market points to an integrated, highly efficient digital-physical hybrid future, expected to hit an aggregate valuation of USD 190 Billion by 2030.
The global apparel market is valued at approximately USD 1.91 trillion in 2026, projected to reach USD 2.54 trillion by 2033, compounding at a stable CAGR of 4.1%.

risks: Apparel and retail undergoing tremendous change
Consumers becoming more discerning
Competition evolving rapidly
Boundaries between physical retail, digital commerce and other channels becoming increasingly fluid
Geopolitical pressures
Elevated interest rates
Supply-side constraints
Energy costs and supply chain stability
Geopolitical hazard premiums pushing energy costs higher
Strategic, financial, liquidity, security, regulatory, legal, reputational and other risks
Mid-premium consumers demand high-end design, flawless fit, and superior fabric, but are highly sensitive to price hikes
Driven by social media and short trend life cycles, consumer preferences change rapidly

Risk for traders who rely on fragmented, unorganized third-party manufacturers is the inability to guarantee fabric quality, ethical labor, or consistent sizing, which can instantly damage brand credibility
High inflation in general living costs means the mid-premium segment—often seen as a discretionary indulgence rather than a necessity

Aggressive Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) and Fast-Fashion Aggregators between Global and domestic fast-fashion giants optimizing their supply chains to churn out ultra-trendy clothes at highly competitive price points
Tariff turbulence: US tariffs are reshaping global trade as higher duties push up costs across the value chain, heavily impacting fashion
In the opinion of the Board, there are no major elements of risk which has the potential of threatening the existence of the Company.
GST balances under reconciliation across multiple state registrations; adjustments may arise upon completion.
Interest due to MSME suppliers for delayed payments (Rs 3.95 crore provided in FY26, Rs 3.94 crore in FY25) though management believes it may not be claimed.
Credit risk from unsecured trade receivables
Liquidity risk managed through committed credit facilities
Interest rate risk on floating rate borrowings
Foreign currency risk primarily from USD exposure on trade payables
Asset volatility and changes in bond yields affecting gratuity plan liabilities
